author: Bobby Grayson
description:
README Layout table, add after the Explore.lean row: | `Leanactors/Replay.lean` | The `replay` executable (`lake build replay`, `.lake/build/bin/replay`): a line script on stdin (`example bank|ttl|lock`, then `deliver <pid> <msg>`, `run <pid>`, `signal`, `down`, `timer <i>`), replayed with `run` (bank, lock) or `runSys` (ttl), printing the final observables in a canonical text form; a choice the model cannot follow is an error, not a silent stop |
README Elixir table, add after the ttl.exs row: | `elixir/fuzz.exs` | Differential fuzz: seeded random scripts replayed in Lean (the `replay` binary) and on the BEAM (the real modules in `elixir/src`), observables compared byte for byte; `--seed S --only N` reproduces a failure |
README Build section, after the check.sh description: add the sentence 'It ends with `elixir elixir/fuzz.exs --seed 1 --runs 200`: 200 seeded random scripts cycling bank, ttl and lock (about 13s), each replayed by the Lean interpreters through the `replay` executable and by the BEAM, exit 1 with the script on the first mismatch.' Also mention `lake build` now builds the `replay` executable too (a default target). 
README, a new paragraph (suggested under the generic-explorer paragraph, title **Differential testing.**): 'The interpreters `run` and `runSys` are also tested against the BEAM. `Leanactors/Replay.lean` is an executable that replays a script of scheduler choices (environment deliveries, actor runs, signal/DOWN/timer firings) on one example and prints the observable part of the final configuration; `elixir/fuzz.exs` generates such scripts at random and drives the same messages into the real modules. The BEAM has its own scheduler, so scripts are built from phases that have a single outcome under any scheduling (one target per phase; the twin waits for the phase to end via `:sys.get_state` queued behind the message, a receive trace, or a DOWN): bank casts, ticks and audits including a tick deferred during a blocking call; ttl puts, asks, the live timer expiring (a real 300ms sleep) and `put 0` killing the cache, with stale-timer firings replayed in Lean only since the BEAM cancelled them; lock ticks expanded through a simulation of the protocol including the grant cascade and one deferred tick per waiting client. Observables: bank balance, each client's last seen value and pending messages; the cache's value, the reader's count, every value the reader received and pending; the lock's holder and queue, each client's phase and pending. Where the two sides legitimately differ (untimed timers, real time, scheduling), the generator is constrained rather than the comparison. Mutants of the BEAM modules (a withdraw off by one, a get ignored, LIFO grant) are caught within the first runs.'
NOTES section 10 (Round 5) bullet: 'Differential fuzzing (node 442): a `replay` executable over `run`/`runSys` and `elixir/fuzz.exs`. The interesting design point is that the BEAM cannot be told which process to run next, so a script is only comparable if every phase has one outcome under any scheduling; the fuzzer's header documents each phase shape and why. Two things surfaced while building it: the ttl comparison must treat stale timers as Lean-only (the model over-approximates the BEAM's cancelled timeouts, as section 6 says) and treat a stalled driver as a possible spurious expiry (retried, counted); and a lock client blocked in a call cannot answer a system message, so its phase is read off the server's queue. The fuzzer is checked for sensitivity with BEAM mutants (not committed): withdraw n<b, get ignored for one value, LIFO grant, each caught in the first runs.'
Counts for the README status line: hand-written Lean files 23 -> 24 (Replay.lean is executable code, not proofs: 0 theorems), lines +312.
